A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GPUDrive, with matching simulator design, experiments, and Appendices A–D. Their text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original simulator-throughput measurements, reinforcement-learning performance, scenario-scaling results, and collision and off-road outcomes.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain original simulation and training results and add sensor-throughput measurements and an analysis of controllable-agent counts.

M1.justification: The Madrona/BVH/road-decimation design, bicycle dynamics, observation modes, rewards, and IPPO approach are retained. Added descriptions of memory allocation and episode termination do not establish that the underlying procedure changed between versions.

E1.justification: Both versions use WOMD for driving simulation and goal-reaching tasks. Larger training subsets change sample counts, while the added sensor-speed experiment compares simulator configurations within the existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The throughput comparison retains original Nocturne, Nocturne parallelized through PufferLib on 16 CPU cores, and Waymax. The ten-scene training comparison still uses Nocturne, and Table 1 retains the same simulator membership.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported training subset for released agents from 500 to 1,000 scenes. V2 adds a radial-filter/LiDAR throughput sweep and a controllable-agent analysis over 512 scenarios. The ten-scene comparison and its Table 2 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds an observation-modality speed comparison across GPU types and parallel-environment counts in Figure 4, plus a controllable-agent distribution in Figure 3. The existing scenario-count scaling analysis and appendix collision/off-road curves are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions average the training comparison across three seeds and list the same seeds, 42, 12, and 67, in Table 2. The added histogram describes variation between scenes; it does not introduce a new uncertainty-estimation procedure for experimental performance.

E6.justification: The central throughput curves are revised, and Waymax's reported memory-limited parallelism changes from 32 to 16 environments. V2 adds the approximately threefold LiDAR speedup and agent-distribution results. Reported training throughput changes from 20 to 30 million steps/hour, released-agent success from 97% to 95%, and Nocturne training speedup from 25–40x to 30–40x. These revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains; the principal training and scenario-scaling plots are retained.

T1.justification: The bicycle-model equations and assumptions in Section 3.2 and Appendix B, and the ASPS formula, are unchanged. Describing Ak as a set rather than a number clarifies notation without changing the metric. No substantive theory or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a fast, data-driven simulator and released RL agents. The introduction replaces 95% goal-reaching on 100 scenes in two hours with 1,000 scenes in 15 hours, while the abstract replaces broadly 'generally capable' agents with the more specific claim of navigating thousands of scenarios.

C2.justification: V2 explains how scene density affects usable CASPS and suggests selecting denser scenes. It adds a mechanism explanation for LiDAR's speed advantage. New Section 4.3 interprets the previously reported approximately 2% unreachable goals as an approximately 98% success ceiling caused by mislabeled road edges.

D1.justification: V2 adds memory-allocation, termination, agent-removal, road-edge handling, nanobind/Gymnasium interface, and Stable Baselines implementation details. Appendix A updates the release from v0.1 to v0.2.0 and the total-compute bound from under 24 to under 2 GPU-days. Appendix C replaces its code link with an anonymization placeholder, although the public link remains elsewhere.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for Gymnasium, nanobind, and Stable Baselines, and qualifies its comparison with Waymax by acknowledging the absence of reactive IDM agents. The broader related-work coverage and positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and most prose are retained. V2 makes localized rewrites, adds feature-description paragraphs and Section 4.3, renames Appendix B, removes the acknowledgments/funding section, and switches to author-year citations.

P2.justification: V2 adds a four-scenario illustration and a sensor-throughput figure, and expands the main throughput display from two panels to three with an agent-count histogram. It corrects the swapped ASPS/CASPS caption descriptions, relabels the observation diagram, reformats Table 1, and resizes the unchanged appendix curves into separated panels with added labels.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the speed claims easier to assess through direct sensor comparisons, corrected ASPS/CASPS descriptions, and evidence about controllable-agent counts. Added implementation details also improve clarity. The gains remain limited: the main learning evidence is retained, and the new 1,000-scene/15-hour claim is not reconciled with the retained 1,024-scene/about-200-minute result.
